family.name: Social Media
family.summary: Engagement that is "up" because of a giveaway whose followers leave, a plan for the next quarter, and a public reply to a viral complaint that would make it worse.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: What is actually working?
stages.summary: Explain what the engagement numbers hide and what actually drives sales. Think aloud: shows whether they look past vanity metrics.

stages.title: Next quarter's plan
stages.summary: Commit to where the quarter's budget goes and estimate the sales impact. Think aloud.

stages.title: Six weeks later
stages.summary: The situation changes based on their plan. Tests whether they adapt and explain what happened.

stages.title: Review a reply to a viral complaint
stages.summary: Critique an intern's public reply to a viral complaint that exposes the customer's details and makes things worse. Think aloud.

stages.title: Reel captions (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write on-brand Reel hooks and captions with any AI tool, and paste the conversation. Shows how they work with AI.

stages.title: A real campaign or post
stages.summary: A real social campaign or post that got attention but didn't help the business. Checks specificity and ownership.

brief.text: You've just joined **Stridez** (@stridez), a running shoe brand, as social media lead. Your predecessor's last report said: **"Engagement rate up from 4.4% to 8.1%, and 17,000 new followers in a month."** The CEO loved it. You have ₹6,00,000 a quarter beyond salaries.

items: Followers went from 61,000 to 80,000 during the giveaway. 72% of the accounts that followed during the giveaway have since unfollowed.
Social sales the month before were ₹1,40,624.
Brand voice: direct and practical: no exclamation marks, no "game-changer", no injury claims.

brief.text: The company and numbers are fictional, and every candidate gets a slightly different version. A calculator is fine.

prompt.text: What is a social media metric you think is overrated, and why?
Keep it under 45 seconds. This one is not scored; it just gets you talking.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: The CEO asks: **"So we should do more giveaways, right?"** What is actually working on your channels, what is not, and what do you tell them?
Refer to specific formats and numbers. The data is on the left.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

choices.label: Put the budget behind boosting the best Reels

prompt.text: Where does most of the ₹6,00,000 go next quarter?
Pick one, then explain why, roughly how much extra social sales you expect a month (and how you got that), and the risk you are accepting.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "A bigger giveaway every month"

prompt.text: The second giveaway added 16,000 followers and the CEO is delighted. But reach per regular post is down 25% and social sales have not moved.
**What do you tell the CEO, and what do you change?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "A paid micro-creator programme"

prompt.text: Of 10 creators, three drove 67% of the tracked sales. One of the others posted about the Tempo 2 running shoe without disclosing it was paid, and a follower has called it out in the comments.
**What do you do this week, and how do you change the programme?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Put the budget behind boosting the best Reels"

prompt.text: Boosted Reels brought sales, but the cost per thousand views is up 41% since week one. The paid-ads team says your boosts are bidding against their campaigns for the same audience.
**What do you do, and what do you agree with the paid-ads team?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "A weekly original video series"

prompt.text: Views are down 41% from episode one to episode five. Episode two did well because it featured a customer. The team is spending two days a week on production.
**Do you continue? What do you change?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

stages.title: Review a reply to a viral complaint

prompt.text: A customer, Meera, posted a video that says the sole came apart after two weeks, and shows the shoe. It has 3,28,000 views and 2,320 comments. An intern drafted the public reply below and wants to post it now.
**Name the three most important problems, most important first, and what you would do instead.** You do not need to comment on every line.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

material.text: Hi Meera, we got back to you within the hour as always. We've looked up order #79363, delivered to 14 Lake View Road, and honestly nobody else has ever reported this, so it is most likely down to how the product was stored or used. To make it right we'll send you a free year of the Tempo 2 running shoe. We've also hidden the negative comments on our page to keep things positive.

prompt.text: Use any AI tool you like for this one. We are assessing how you use it, not whether you do.
Write the opening hook (the first line on screen) and caption for three Reels about the Tempo 2 running shoe. Follow the brand voice in the brief.

items: Paste your full AI conversation, or write "none".
In 2–3 lines, say what you kept, changed or rejected from the AI and why.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **Tell us about a social campaign or post that got attention but did not help the business, or went wrong.** What did you see, what did you do, and what would you do differently?
Specifics such as numbers and timelines matter more than polish.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.
